method.kind: direct OpenAI-compatible request cache isolation probe
method.system_prefix: Same synthetic system string repeated 700 times; exact text not retained.
sequence: A0: one read_file schema, user text A
TOOLS_CHANGED: same messages, add one edit_file schema
TOOLS_CHANGED_REPEAT: exact repeat of changed-tool request
MESSAGE_CHANGED: original read_file schema, change only user text
MESSAGE_CHANGED_REPEAT: exact repeat of changed-message request
method.payload_retention: No raw prompt, tool schema, or model response content retained.

findings: An exact repeated request reused all but four prompt tokens.
Changing only the tool schema list after the long stable system and identical messages resulted in zero cached prompt tokens.
Changing only the user message while restoring the original tool list retained 17260 cached tokens, showing the long static prefix remained reusable across this message change.
The same values were observed on Ollama 0.40.0 and 0.40.1.
The leading explanation for HADES' diagnosis-to-action cache miss is now the changed tool schema list being rendered before the reusable prompt prefix on this Ollama/model path.
limitations: One controlled sequence, not a repeated statistical benchmark.
Direct Ollama API requests, not Hermes-generated multi-turn requests; this isolates schema behavior but does not fully reproduce HADES transcript serialization.
The tool-list change appended a second schema; it models a changed catalog but not every HADES schema layout.
This does not establish whether the effect is specific to Qwen's template or applies to other models/runtimes.
No latency or owner-preference conclusion is drawn.
